Exam Type: MRI KNEE RIGHT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Intermittent pain walking up and down the steps for one month.
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the right knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.. Tricompartmental marginal osteophytes.

JOINT SPACE:
Moderate joint effusion with synovitis. No intra-articular bodies. Trace Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Complex tear medial meniscus posterior root, posterior horn, and body including a radial tear at the posterior root with moderate extrusion of the body into the meniscotibial recess.
Medial compartment cartilage: Full thickness cartilage denudation throughout the medial weightbearing surfaces with subchondral cystic change marrow edema.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Degenerative/globular signal at the posterior root lateral meniscus without tearing.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Mild cartilage heterogeneity fissuring.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Full thickness cartilage loss and medial patellar facet extending to the median ridge with subchondral marrow edema at the median ridge. High-grade cartilage loss at the medial trochlea.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 10 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
1.	Complex tear medial meniscus posterior root, posterior horn, and body including a radial tear at the posterior root with moderate extrusion of the body into the meniscotibial recess.
2.	Tricompartmental osteoarthritis, severe in the medial and patellofemoral compartment.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Pain.
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
Small joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. Small Baker cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Medial compartment cartilage: There is mild to moderate cartilage thinning and fissuring most prominent at the posterior weightbearing aspect of the medial femoral condyle.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: There is mild to moderate cartilage thinning and surface irregularity, most prominent at the posterior weightbearing aspect.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: There is a full-thickness cartilage delamination defect at the inferior aspect of the lateral patellar facet, measuring 1.0 cm in diameter. Cartilage delamination and flap formation is also noted at the lateral and central trochlea, measuring approximately 1.7 cm in diameter.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 8 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:

1. Tricompartmental chondrosis, most prominent in the patellofemoral compartment with areas of full-thickness cartilage delamination and flap formation.

2. Small joint effusion. Small Baker cyst.

In medial compartment, there is focal high grade chondrosis (more than 50% thickness cartilage loss) at the posteromedial tibial plateau (about 1.3* 1.6 cm). There is radial tear at the posterior horn of the medial meniscus. 
 In lateral compartment, there is longitudinal vertical tear with intact3 cm intrameniscal cyst at the anterior horn of the lateral meniscus. 
 Chronic complete tear of the anterior cruciate ligament at mid substance.  
 The medial and lateral ligamentous complexes are intact. Minimal effusion is present in right knee.  Focal high grade chondrosis (more than 50% thickness cartilage loss) at the posteromedial tibial plateau (about 1.3* 1.6 cm), right knee. 
  Radial tear at the posterior horn of the medial meniscus. 
  Longitudinal vertical tear with intact3 cm intrameniscal cyst at the anterior horn of the lateral meniscus. 
  Chronic complete tear of the anterior cruciate ligament at mid substance.  
  Minimal effusion in right knee.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE RIGHT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication:  Knee pain.. 
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:  Multiplanar and multisequence MRI of the right  knee without IV contrast.   

FINDINGS: 

JOINT EFFUSION:  Moderate knee joint effusion. Small popliteal cyst. 

ANTERIOR CRUCIATE LIGAMENT:  Intact. 

POSTERIOR CRUCIATE LIGAMENT:  Intact. 

MEDIAL MENISCUS: Intact. 

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:  Within normal limits. 

LATERAL MENISCUS:  Diminutive appearance of the posterior body and posterior horn of the medial meniscus suggestive of large radial tear in the absence of previous meniscectomy.

The meniscal body also demonstrates complex tearing involving the free edge and the undersurface.

Intrasubstance degeneration in the anterior horn. 

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:  High-grade and full-thickness cartilage loss involving the central to posterior aspects of the femoral condyle and tibial plateau, with mild subchondral edema. Small central and marginal osteophytes. 

MEDIAL COLLATERAL LIGAMENT:  Intact.

LATERAL COLLATERAL LIGAMENT COMPLEX:  Intact.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT: Diffuse mild thinning of the patellar cartilage. There is high-grade and full-thickness cartilage loss throughout the trochlea, maximal centrally and laterally, with multifocal subchondral bone marrow edema. 

EXTENSOR APPARATUS:  Quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact. 

BONE MARROW:  No fracture. 
 
OTHER:  None. 


IMPRESSION:

1. Diminutive appearance of the posterior body and posterior horn of the lateral meniscus, suggestive of large radial tear in the absence of previous meniscectomy.

2. Moderate lateral and patellofemoral compartment osteoarthritis.

3. Moderate knee joint effusion and small popliteal cyst.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE RIGHT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Medial knee pain. Positive medial meniscus testing. 
Comparison: [REDACTED]. 

TECHNIQUE:  Multiplanar and multisequence MRI of the right  knee without IV contrast.   

FINDINGS: 

JOINT EFFUSION:  Moderate knee joint effusion. No popliteal cyst. 

ANTERIOR CRUCIATE LIGAMENT:  Intact. 

POSTERIOR CRUCIATE LIGAMENT:  Intact. 

MEDIAL MENISCUS: High-grade radial tear at the posterior horn/root junction. Large degree of peripheral meniscal extrusion, with the meniscus projecting 5 mm beyond the tibial margin. There is also a horizontal tear of the meniscal body and oblique undersurface tear of the posterior horn. 

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:  There is full-thickness cartilage loss involving the weightbearing portions of the femoral condyle and tibial plateau, with mild to moderate subchondral bone marrow edema. 

LATERAL MENISCUS:  Intact.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:  Within normal limits. 

MEDIAL COLLATERAL LIGAMENT:  Bowing of the ligament secondary to meniscal extrusion. 

LATERAL COLLATERAL LIGAMENT COMPLEX:  Intact.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT: Diffuse thinning of the patellar cartilage, with high-grade and small full-thickness cartilage loss in the medial patellar facet. There is also multifocal cartilage fissuring of the lateral patellar facet. Partial-thickness cartilage loss is noted in the central and medial aspect of the trochlea. 

EXTENSOR APPARATUS:  Quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact. 

BONE MARROW:  No fracture. 
 
OTHER:  None. 


IMPRESSION:

1. Complex tear of the medial meniscus, including radial tear at the posterior horn/root junction, with peripheral extrusion.

2. Moderate medial greater than patellofemoral compartment osteoarthritis.

3. Moderate knee joint effusion.
